title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — गुणत्रयविभागयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 14: The Three Qualities
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/गुणत्रयविभागयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

sentences.t:
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥

param bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānām jñānam uttamam |
yat jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parām siddhim itaḥ gatāḥ ||

sentences.l: Supreme, again I shall declare — of-knowledges the knowledge, best — having known which, all sages have gone hence to supreme perfection.
sentences.i: I shall speak once more of the supreme knowledge, the best among knowledges, by knowing which all the sages have attained the highest perfection.
sentences.n: This chapter opens with no question from Arjuna; Kṛṣṇa simply continues speaking, and bhūyaḥ, 'again, further', signals that what follows continues and completes the teaching on prakṛti and puruṣa begun in chapter 13. Jñānānāṃ jñānam uttamam, 'the best knowledge among knowledges' (a partitive genitive), anticipates the doctrine of the three guṇas that occupies the rest of the chapter, and para, 'supreme', already used of brahman at 13.17, is here applied to this teaching itself. Sandhi: yajjñātvā is yat+jñātvā (-t+j-→-j j-); siddhim ito packs siddhim+itaḥ (simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel) and itaḥ+gatāḥ (-aḥ before g-→-o).

sentences.t:
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः ।
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
sentences.tr:
idam jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ |
sarge api na upajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca ||

knowledge (acc. sg. neut., object of upāśritya; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to resort to, rely upon (upāśritya: gerund 'having relied upon')
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my')

sentences.l: This knowledge having relied upon, [they] have come to my same-nature; at creation too they are not born, and at dissolution they are not disturbed.
sentences.i: Relying on this knowledge, they have come to share my own nature; they are not born even at a new creation, nor are they troubled at its dissolution.
sentences.n: Sādharmya, 'sameness of nature/dharma [with me]', names the goal already promised in these very terms at 13.18's mad-bhāvāya: those who grasp this knowledge cease to be swept up in the endless cycle of sarga and pralaya, 'creation' and 'dissolution', that governs ordinary souls born again at every new world-age. Sandhi: sarge'pi is sarge+api (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha); nopajāyante is na+upajāyante (-a+u-→-o-).

sentences.t:
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् ।
संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
mama yoniḥ mahat brahma tasmin garbham dadhāmi aham |
saṃbhavaḥ sarva-bhūtānām tataḥ bhavati bhārata ||

great (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma; -t+b-→-d b-)

sentences.l: My womb [is] the-great-brahman; in that I place the-germ. The-origination of-all-beings comes from-that, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: The great brahman is my womb; in it I place the seed. From that, Bhārata, comes the coming-into-being of every creature.
sentences.n: This opens a brief cosmogony (continued at verse 4): mahad brahma, 'the great brahman' — here primordial, unevolved nature (prakṛti), not the transcendent brahman described at 13.12-17 — receives Kṛṣṇa's garbham, 'germ, seed', the act of insemination from which all beings arise. Sandhi: yonir mahad brahma packs yoniḥ+mahat (-iḥ+m-→-ir m-) and mahat+brahma (-t+b-→-d b-); dadhāmy ahaṃ is dadhāmi+aham (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः संभवन्ति याः ।
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
tāsām brahma mahat-yoniḥ aham bīja-pradaḥ pitā ||

'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
form, embodiment (nom. pl. fem., subject)
to arise, come into being (saṃbhavanti: present 3rd pl. 'arise')
which (yāḥ: nom. pl. fem. relative)
those, they (tāsām: gen. pl. fem. 'of them', referring to the mūrtayaḥ)
brahman, the absolute, kept untranslated per convention (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
great (first compound member, undeclined stem before the following vowel; -t+y-→-d y-)
womb, matrix (mahad-yoniḥ: 'the great womb', nom. sg. fem., predicate of brahma; -iḥ+a-→-ir a-)
I (nom. sg., subject of the next clause)
seed (first compound member)
giving, bestowing (from pra-dā; bīja-prada: 'seed-giving', nom. sg. masc., in apposition with pitā)
father (nom. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: In-all-wombs, O Kaunteya, whatever forms arise — of-them, brahman [is] the-great-womb; I [am] the-seed-giving father.
sentences.i: Whatever forms come to be in any womb, Kaunteya, brahman is their great womb, and I am the father who supplies the seed.
sentences.n: This completes the cosmogony of verse 3: every mūrti, 'form, embodiment', born in any yoni, 'womb' (any species, any realm), has mahad brahma for its universal matrix, with Kṛṣṇa as bīja-pradaḥ pitā, 'the seed-giving father' — the same pairing of matter as womb and spirit as begetter that verses 5 onward recast as the guṇas of prakṛti binding the puruṣa. Sandhi: mahadyonir ahaṃ packs mahat+yoniḥ (-t+y-→-d y-) and yoniḥ+aham (-iḥ+a-→-ir a-).

sentences.t:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ।
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
sattvam rajaḥ tamaḥ iti guṇāḥ prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam ||

morph.gloss: sattva, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut., in apposition, one of the three guṇas named)
rajas, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut.; -aḥ+t-→-as t- before tamaḥ)
tamas, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut.; visarga elided before the following vowel i- of iti)
thus (closing the list of the three names)
quality, the guṇas, kept untranslated (nom. pl. masc., subject)
nature (first compound member)
arisen, originating (saṃbhava: 'arisen from', prakṛti-saṃbhava: 'born of nature', nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with guṇāḥ)
to bind (nibadhnanti: present 3rd pl. 'they bind')
great (first compound member)
arm (mahā-bāhu: 'mighty-armed', vocative sg., epithet of Arjuna)
body (loc. sg. 'in the body')
the embodied one, the soul (from deha; acc. sg. masc., object of nibadhnanti; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
imperishable (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with dehinam)

sentences.l: Sattva, rajas, tamas — thus [named], the-guṇas, born-of-nature, bind, O mighty-armed one, in-the-body the-imperishable embodied-one.
sentences.i: Sattva, rajas, and tamas — these are the guṇas that arise from nature; they bind the imperishable soul, mighty-armed one, within the body.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's central teaching, naming all three guṇas together for the first time in the poem (individual guṇas were named earlier, e.g. 7.12-13, but not defined until here) and stating at once their basic effect: to nibadhnanti, 'bind', the dehin, the otherwise avyaya, 'imperishable', embodied self, within the deha, 'body'. Verses 6-8 define each guṇa in turn; verses 9-13 describe their interplay. Sandhi: rajastama is rajaḥ+tamaḥ (-aḥ+t-→-as t-), with tamaḥ's own visarga then eliding before the following vowel i- of iti (as already at 13.1's kṣetrajña iti); dehinam avyayam is simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel.

sentences.t:
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
sentences.tr:
tatra sattvam nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam |
sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena ca anagha ||

morph.gloss: there, among these (adverb, referring back to the guṇas just named)
sattva, kept untranslated (nom. sg. neut., subject)
stainlessness, purity (nirmalatvāt: abl. sg. 'because of its stainlessness')
illuminating, radiant (prakāśaka: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
free from affliction, untainted, healthy (nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
happiness, pleasure (first compound member)
attachment, contact (sukha-saṅga: 'attachment to happiness', instr. sg.)
to bind (badhnāti: present 3rd sg. 'binds')
knowledge (first compound member)
attachment (jñāna-saṅga: 'attachment to knowledge', instr. sg.)
and (ca+anagha→cānagha, a+a→ā)
blameless, sinless (anagha: vocative sg., epithet of Arjuna)

sentences.l: There, sattva, because-of-[its]-stainlessness illuminating, unafflicted, binds through attachment-to-happiness and through attachment-to-knowledge, O blameless one.
sentences.i: Of these, sattva, being stainless, is luminous and untainted; yet it binds through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, blameless one.
sentences.n: The first of the three definitions (continued at verses 7-8): sattva, nirmalatvāt, 'because of its stainlessness', is prakāśaka, 'illuminating' (a recurring image for sattva, echoed of brahman itself at 13.17), yet even sattva binds — through sukha-saṅga and jñāna-saṅga, 'attachment to happiness' and 'attachment to knowledge'. That a taste for knowledge itself can bind is a pointed warning, anticipated by verse 17's own sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam. Sandhi: cānagha is ca+anagha (a+a→ā); nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam runs on as one fused token, its final -m before the actual next word's consonant p- unaffected.

sentences.t:
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
sentences.tr:
rajaḥ rāga-ātmakam viddhi tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam |
tat nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena dehinam ||

passion, desire (first compound member; rāga+ātmaka→rāgātmaka, a+ā→ā)
having the nature of, consisting of (rāga-ātmaka: 'of the nature of passion', acc. sg. neut., predicate complement of viddhi)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!')
craving, thirst (first compound member)

arisen, originating (samudbhava: 'arisen from', tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhava: 'arising from craving and attachment', acc. sg. neut., predicate complement)
that, it (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject, referring to rajas; -t+n-→-n n-)
to bind (nibadhnāti: present 3rd sg. 'binds')
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
action (first compound member)

the embodied one, the soul (acc. sg. masc., object of nibadhnāti)

sentences.l: Rajas, of-the-nature-of-passion, know, arisen-from-craving-and-attachment; that binds, O Kaunteya, through attachment-to-action, the-embodied-one.
sentences.i: Know rajas to be passionate by nature, arising from craving and attachment; it binds the embodied soul, Kaunteya, through attachment to action.
sentences.n: The second definition: rajas is rāgātmakam, 'of the nature of passion', traced to tṛṣṇā and saṅga, 'craving' and 'attachment' — terms that recur through this chapter as the diagnostic vocabulary for what binds. Where sattva bound through happiness and knowledge, rajas binds karma-saṅgena, 'through attachment to action', restating in this chapter's own terms the teaching on niṣkāma karma of chapters 2-3. Sandhi: rāgātmakaṃ is rāga+ātmakam (a+ā→ā); tannibadhnāti is tat+nibadhnāti (-t+n-→-n n-).

sentences.t:
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
tamaḥ tu ajñāna-jam viddhi mohanam sarva-dehinām |
pramāda-ālasya-nidrābhiḥ tat nibadhnāti bhārata ||

all (first compound member)

laziness, sloth (second member)
sleep (nidrābhiḥ: instr. pl., 'through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep'; -iḥ+t-→-is t-)
that, it (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject, referring to tamas; -t+n-→-n n-)
to bind (nibadhnāti: present 3rd sg. 'binds')
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: Tamas, but, born-of-ignorance, know, deluding of-all-embodied-beings; through heedlessness-laziness-and-sleep, that binds, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: But know tamas to be born of ignorance, the deluder of every embodied creature; it binds through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep, Bhārata.
sentences.n: The third definition completes the set: tamas is ajñānajam, 'born of ignorance' (contrasted with rajas's passion and sattva's stainless light), and mohanam, 'deluding'; its binding instruments are named as a compact triad, pramāda, ālasya, nidrā, 'heedlessness, laziness, sleep', whose negation (apramāda) will recur as a mark of the sattvic and the divine at 16.3. Sandhi: tamastv ajñānajaṃ packs tamaḥ+tu (-aḥ+t-→-as t-) and tu+ajñānajam (yaṇ sandhi, -u+a-→-v a-); pramādālasya- is pramāda+ālasya (a+ā→ā); nidrābhis tannibadhnāti packs nidrābhiḥ+tat (-iḥ+t-→-is t-) and tat+nibadhnāti (-t+n-→-n n-).

sentences.t:
सत्त्वं सुखे संजयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे संजयत्युत ॥
sentences.tr:
sattvam sukhe saṃjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde saṃjayati uta ||

to attach, cling (causative saṃjayati: present 3rd sg. 'attaches, binds')

action (loc. sg. 'to action')

to cover, envelop (āvṛtya: gerund 'having covered')
but

to attach, cling (causative saṃjayati: present 3rd sg. 'attaches'; -i+u-→-y u-)

sentences.l: Sattva attaches to-happiness, rajas to-action, O Bhārata; knowledge having-covered, but, tamas to-heedlessness attaches indeed.
sentences.i: Sattva attaches one to happiness, rajas to action, Bhārata; but tamas, covering over knowledge, attaches one instead to heedlessness.
sentences.n: This turns from defining each guṇa to how each is felt from within: each guṇa saṃjayati, 'attaches, binds', its subject to a characteristic state — sattva to sukha, rajas to karman, and tamas, having first āvṛtya, 'covered over', jñāna (an eclipse-like image that recurs at verse 17's tamaso bhavato'jñānam), to pramāda. Sandhi: jñānam āvṛtya is simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel; saṃjayaty uta is saṃjayati+uta (-i+u-→-y u-).

sentences.t:
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत ।
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥

sentences.l: Rajas-and-tamas having overcome, sattva prevails, O Bhārata; rajas sattva and-tamas-indeed, tamas sattva and-rajas likewise.
sentences.i: Sattva prevails, Bhārata, having overcome rajas and tamas; so too rajas prevails, overcoming sattva and tamas, and tamas, overcoming sattva and rajas.
sentences.n: This describes the guṇas' ceaseless rivalry (developed further at verses 11-13's symptoms of each guṇa's ascendancy): whichever is momentarily dominant does so by abhibhūya, 'having overcome', the other two. The second line is deliberately compressed, carrying over bhavati and abhibhūya from the first line by ellipsis into two further implied clauses — a terse listing typical of this chapter's more aphoristic verses. Sandhi: rajastamaścābhibhūya packs rajaḥ+tamaḥ (-aḥ+t-→-as t-), tamaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-), and ca+abhibhūya (a+a→ā); tamaścaiva packs tamaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) and ca+eva (a+e→ai); rajastathā is rajaḥ+tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-).

sentences.t:
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते ।
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-dvāreṣu dehe asmin prakāśaḥ upajāyate |
jñānam yadā tadā vidyāt vivṛddham sattvam iti uta ||

morph.gloss: all (first compound member)
gate, door (sarva-dvāra: loc. pl. 'in all the gates', i.e. the senses)
body (dehe: loc. sg. 'in the body'; -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
this (asmin: loc. sg., agreeing with dehe; simply written joined, the nasal unaffected before the following consonant p-)
light, illumination (prakāśa: nom. sg. masc., subject; visarga elided before the following vowel u- of the next word)
to be born, arise (upajāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'arises')
knowledge (nom. sg. neut., subject, with upajāyate understood, in apposition with prakāśaḥ)
when (relative adverb)
then (correlative adverb)
to know (vidyāt: optative 3rd sg. 'one should know'; -t+v-→-d v-)
increased, grown predominant (vivṛddha: past participle, acc. sg. neut., predicate complement)
sattva, kept untranslated (acc. sg. neut., object of vidyāt; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
thus (quotation particle; iti+uta→ity uta, -i+u-→-y u-)
indeed

sentences.l: In-all-the-gates, in-this body, illumination arises; knowledge — when, then, one-should-know increased sattva, indeed.
sentences.i: When illumination arises at every gate of this body, then one should know that sattva has grown predominant.
sentences.n: This gives the diagnostic sign of sattva's ascendancy, paralleled for rajas and tamas at verses 12-13: sarva-dvāreṣu, 'at all the gates' (the senses, pictured as doorways of the body, as already at 5.13's sarva-dvāreṣu dehe), prakāśa arising is the mark that sattva has grown vivṛddham, 'increased, predominant'. Sandhi: dehe'sminprakāśa packs dehe+asmin (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha) and asmin+prakāśaḥ (simply joined before the consonant p-, prakāśaḥ's own visarga then eliding before the following vowel u- of upajāyate); vidyād vivṛddhaṃ is vidyāt+vivṛddham (-t+v-→-d v-); sattvam ity uta packs sattvam+iti (simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel) and iti+uta (-i+u-→-y u-).

sentences.t:
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
sentences.tr:
lobhaḥ pravṛttiḥ ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā |
rajasi etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharata-ṛṣabha ||

morph.gloss: greed (nom. sg. masc., subject)
activity, engagement (pravṛtti: nom. sg. fem.; -iḥ+ā-→-ir ā-)
undertaking, initiative (ārambha: nom. sg. masc.)
action (karmaṇām: gen. pl. 'of actions'; simply written joined, the ending -m unaffected before the vowel)
restlessness, lack of tranquility (nom. sg. masc.)
desire, longing (nom. sg. fem.)
rajas, kept untranslated (rajasi: loc. sg. 'in rajas'; -i+e-→-y e-)
this (etāni: nom. pl. neut., subject, referring to the qualities just listed)
to arise, be born (jāyante: present middle 3rd pl. 'arise')
increased, grown predominant (vivṛddha: past participle, loc. sg., agreeing with an implied rajasi, locative absolute: 'when [rajas] has increased')
Bharata, the Kuru ancestor (first compound member; bharata+ṛṣabha→bharatarṣabha, -a+ṛ-→-ar-)
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative, epithet of Arjuna)

sentences.l: Greed, activity, undertaking-of-actions, restlessness, longing — these arise, in-rajas, when increased, O bull-among-the-Bharatas.
sentences.i: Greed, engagement, the taking up of actions, restlessness, longing — these arise when rajas has grown predominant, bull among the Bharatas.
sentences.n: The symptoms of rajas's ascendancy, matching sattva's single sign at verse 11 with a fivefold list: lobha, 'greed'; pravṛtti, 'activity'; ārambha, 'undertaking [of action]'; aśama, 'restlessness'; spṛhā, 'longing' — the cluster of qualities driving restless action already diagnosed as rajas's danger in chapters 2-3. Sandhi: pravṛttir ārambhaḥ is pravṛttiḥ+ārambhaḥ (-iḥ+ā-→-ir ā-); rajasyetāni is rajasi+etāni (-i+e-→-y e-); vivṛddhe is a locative-absolute participle agreeing with an unexpressed rajasi, 'when [rajas] has increased' — the same construction recurs, with tamasi, at verse 13.

sentences.t:
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
sentences.tr:
aprakāśaḥ apravṛttiḥ ca pramādaḥ mohaḥ eva ca |
tamasi etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kuru-nandana ||

morph.gloss: lack of illumination, absence of light (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
inactivity, lack of initiative (nom. sg. fem.; -iḥ+c-→-iś c-)
and
heedlessness, negligence (nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m-→-o)
delusion, confusion (moha: nom. sg. masc.; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)
indeed
and
tamas, kept untranslated (tamasi: loc. sg. 'in tamas'; -i+e-→-y e-)
this (etāni: nom. pl. neut., subject)
to arise, be born (jāyante: present middle 3rd pl. 'arise')
increased, grown predominant (vivṛddha: past participle, loc. sg., agreeing with an implied tamasi, locative absolute: 'when [tamas] has increased')
the Kuru clan (first compound member)
joy, delight (kuru-nandana: 'joy of the Kurus', vocative, epithet of Arjuna)

sentences.l: Lack-of-illumination and inactivity, heedlessness, and delusion indeed — these arise, in-tamas, when increased, O joy-of-the-Kurus.
sentences.i: Lack of light, inertia, heedlessness, and delusion — these arise when tamas has grown predominant, joy of the Kurus.
sentences.n: The symptoms of tamas's ascendancy, in parallel with verses 11-12: aprakāśa, 'lack of illumination' (the negation of sattva's own mark from verse 11), apravṛtti, 'inactivity' (the negation of rajas's pravṛtti from verse 12), pramāda, 'heedlessness' (tamas's own binding-instrument, named already at verse 8), and moha, 'delusion'. Sandhi: aprakāśo'pravṛttiś ca packs aprakāśaḥ+apravṛttiḥ (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha) and apravṛttiḥ+ca (-iḥ+c-→-iś c-); moha eva shows the visarga of mohaḥ eliding before the following vowel e-; tamasyetāni is tamasi+etāni (-i+e-→-y e-), matching verse 12's rajasyetāni.

sentences.t:
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayam yāti deha-bhṛt |
tadā uttama-vidām lokān amalān pratipadyate ||

morph.gloss: when (relative adverb)
sattva, kept untranslated (loc. sg. 'in sattva')
increased, grown predominant (pravṛddha: past participle, loc. sg., agreeing with sattve: locative absolute, 'when sattva has increased')
but, now
dissolution, death (acc. sg., object of yāti)
to go (yāti: present 3rd sg. 'goes')
body (first compound member)
bearer (from bhṛ; deha-bhṛt: 'the bearer of the body', i.e. the embodied soul, nom. sg. masc., subject)
then (tadā+uttama→tadottama, ā+u→o)
highest, supreme (first compound member)
knowing, one who knows (uttama-vid: 'knower of the highest', vidām: gen. pl. 'of those who know the highest')
world (lokān: acc. pl. masc., object of pratipadyate; simply written joined with the following word)
stainless, spotless (amalān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with lokān)
to attain, reach (pratipadyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains')

sentences.l: When in-sattva-increased, but, to-dissolution goes the-body-bearer, then to-the-worlds-of-those-who-know-the-highest, stainless, he attains.
sentences.i: But when the embodied one dies while sattva predominates, he attains to the stainless worlds of those who know the highest.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's account of destiny after death, keyed to whichever guṇa predominates at the moment of dying (continued at verse 15 for rajas and tamas): deha-bhṛt, 'the body-bearer', dying sattve pravṛddhe, 'when sattva has increased' (a locative absolute), reaches uttama-vidāṃ lokān amalān, 'the stainless worlds of those who know the highest' — recasting, in the guṇas' own terms, the teaching on the paths after death already given at 8.23-26. Sandhi: tadottamavidāṃ is tadā+uttama-vidām (ā+u→o); lokān amalān and amalān pratipadyate are both simply written joined, within one long fused compound token.

sentences.t:
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते ।
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥
sentences.tr:
rajasi pralayam gatvā karma-saṅgiṣu jāyate |
tathā pralīnaḥ tamasi mūḍha-yoniṣu jāyate ||

morph.gloss: rajas, kept untranslated (loc. sg. 'in rajas', implying death while rajas predominates)
dissolution, death (acc. sg., object of gatvā)
to go (gatvā: gerund 'having gone', i.e. having died)
action (first compound member)
attached to, clinging to (karma-saṅgin: 'attached to action', loc. pl. 'among those attached to action')
to arise, be born (jāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'is born')
likewise, so
dissolved, dead (pralīna: past participle, nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
tamas, kept untranslated (tamasi: loc. sg. 'in tamas')
confused, deluded, foolish (from muh, first compound member)
womb (mūḍha-yoni: 'wombs of the deluded', loc. pl.)
to arise, be born (jāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'is born')

sentences.l: Having-gone to-dissolution in-rajas, among-those-attached-to-action he is born; likewise, one-dissolved in-tamas, in-wombs-of-the-deluded he is born.
sentences.i: One who dies while rajas predominates is born among those attached to action; and one who dies in tamas is born among the deluded.
sentences.n: This completes verses 14-15's threefold account of rebirth by guṇa: dying rajasi, 'in rajas', one is born karma-saṅgiṣu, 'among those attached to action' (a fittingly restless destiny for rajas's own besetting attachment, named already at verse 7); dying tamasi, 'in tamas', one is born mūḍha-yoniṣu, 'in wombs of the deluded' — the lowest of the three destinies, matching verse 18's ranking of the guṇas as high, middle, and low. Sandhi: pralīnas tamasi is pralīnaḥ+tamasi (-aḥ+t-→-as t-).

sentences.t:
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् ।
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
sentences.tr:
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasya āhuḥ sāttvikam nirmalam phalam |
rajasaḥ tu phalam duḥkham ajñānam tamasaḥ phalam ||

morph.gloss: action (gen. sg. 'of action')
well-done, good (sukṛta: gen. sg. neut. 'of a good [action]'; sukṛtasya+āhuḥ→sukṛtasyāhuḥ, a+ā→ā)
to say (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present, 'they say')
belonging to sattva, of the nature of sattva (acc. sg. neut., predicate complement; sattva kept untranslated per convention)
stainless, pure (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with phalam)
fruit, result (acc. sg. neut., object of āhuḥ)
rajas, kept untranslated (gen. sg. 'of rajas'; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
but
fruit, result (nom. sg. neut., subject)
pain, suffering (nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
ignorance (nom. sg. neut., predicate of the next clause)
tamas, kept untranslated (gen. sg. 'of tamas')
fruit, result (nom. sg. neut., subject)

sentences.l: Of-action, well-done, they say, of-sattva, stainless, [is] the-fruit; of-rajas, but, the-fruit [is] pain; ignorance [is] the-fruit of-tamas.
sentences.i: The fruit of a good action, they say, is sattva's own, and stainless; the fruit of rajas is suffering; the fruit of tamas is ignorance.
sentences.n: This states the fruit (phala) proper to each guṇa's characteristic action: sukṛta, 'good, well-done [action]', yields a phalam that is sāttvikam nirmalam, 'sattva-natured and stainless'; rajas's fruit is duḥkham, 'pain' (the cost of its restless activity, cf. 18.24's rājasa karma as bahv-āyāsam, 'much toil'); tamas's fruit is simply ajñānam, 'ignorance' — deeds done in delusion produce nothing but more delusion. Sandhi: sukṛtasyāhuḥ is sukṛtasya+āhuḥ (a+ā→ā); rajasastu is rajasaḥ+tu (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); duḥkham ajñānaṃ is simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel.

sentences.t:
सत्त्वात्संजायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
sentences.tr:
sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam rajasaḥ lobhaḥ eva ca |
pramāda-mohau tamasaḥ bhavataḥ ajñānam eva ca ||

morph.gloss: sattva, kept untranslated (sattvāt: abl. sg. 'from sattva')
to arise, come into being (saṃjāyate: present middle 3rd sg. 'arises')
knowledge (nom. sg. neut., subject)
rajas, kept untranslated (abl. sg. 'from rajas'; -aḥ before l-→-o)
greed (nom. sg. masc., subject; visarga elided before the following vowel e-)
indeed
and
heedlessness, negligence (first compound member)
delusion (pramāda-moha: nom. dual, subject, 'heedlessness and delusion')
tamas, kept untranslated (abl. sg. 'from tamas'; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
to be, become (bhavataḥ: present 3rd dual 'arise'; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
ignorance (nom. sg. neut., subject, joined to the pair by ca; simply written joined with eva, -m unaffected before the vowel)
indeed
and

sentences.l: From-sattva arises knowledge, from-rajas greed indeed, and; heedlessness-and-delusion from-tamas arise, and ignorance too, and.
sentences.i: From sattva arises knowledge, from rajas greed; from tamas arise heedlessness and delusion, and ignorance as well.
sentences.n: This names the psychological products of each guṇa, paralleling verse 16's fruits of action: sattva yields jñānam, 'knowledge' (though verse 6 has already warned that even attachment to this knowledge can bind); rajas yields lobha, 'greed' (echoing verse 12's lobhaḥ as rajas's first symptom); tamas yields pramāda-mohau, 'heedlessness and delusion' (again echoing verses 8 and 13), and ajñānam, 'ignorance', closing the list where tamas also began, since ignorance is both its origin (verse 8's ajñānajam) and its fruit. Sandhi: sattvātsaṃjāyate is simply written joined (both dental consonants, no change); rajaso is rajasaḥ, -aḥ before l-→-o; lobha eva shows the visarga of lobhaḥ eliding before the vowel e-; tamaso is tamasaḥ, -aḥ before bh-→-o; bhavato'jñānam eva packs bhavataḥ+ajñānam (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha) and ajñānam+eva (simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel).

sentences.t:
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥
sentences.tr:
ūrdhvam gacchanti sattva-sthāḥ madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ |
jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthāḥ adhaḥ gacchanti tāmasāḥ ||

morph.gloss: upward, above (ūrdhvam: adverbial acc.)
to go (gacchanti: present 3rd pl. 'they go')
sattva, kept untranslated (first compound member)
abiding in, situated in (sattva-stha: 'abiding in sattva', nom. pl. masc., subject)
the middle (loc. sg. 'in the middle')
to stand, remain (tiṣṭhanti: present 3rd pl. 'they remain')
belonging to rajas, of the nature of rajas (nom. pl. masc., subject; rajas kept untranslated per convention)
lowest, last (first compound member)
quality, guṇa, kept untranslated (second member)
operation, function, mode of activity (third member)

abiding in, situated in (jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-stha: 'abiding in the operation of the lowest guṇa', nom. pl. masc., subject; the vulgate reading, followed here — the BORI critical edition reads jaghanyaguṇavṛttasthāḥ instead, with vṛtta 'state, turn' rather than vṛtti 'operation, function': 'situated in the state of the lowest guṇa' — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint)
downward, below (adhaḥ: adverb; -aḥ before g-→-o)
to go (gacchanti: present 3rd pl. 'they go')
belonging to tamas, of the nature of tamas (nom. pl. masc., subject; tamas kept untranslated per convention)

sentences.l: Upward go those-abiding-in-sattva; in-the-middle stand those-of-rajas; those-abiding-in-the-operation-of-the-lowest-guṇa go downward, those-of-tamas.
sentences.i: Those established in sattva rise upward; those of rajas remain in the middle; those abiding in the lowest guṇa's operation, the ones of tamas, sink downward.
sentences.n: This closes the chapter's account of the guṇas' effects with a ranked cosmology matching verses 14-15's account of rebirth: sattva-sthāḥ, 'those abiding in sattva', go ūrdhvam, 'upward'; rājasāḥ, 'those of rajas', remain madhye, 'in the middle'; and tāmasāḥ, 'those of tamas', described as jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthāḥ, 'abiding in the operation of the lowest guṇa' (jaghanya, 'last, lowest', marking tamas as bottom of the three), go adhaḥ, 'downward'. The vulgate text, followed here, reads jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthāḥ, with vṛtti, 'operation, function'; the BORI critical edition instead reads jaghanyaguṇavṛttasthāḥ, with vṛtta, 'turn, state, condition', in its place — 'situated in the state of the lowest guṇa' rather than 'in its operation' — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint, though the sense is barely affected either way. Sandhi: adho is adhaḥ, -aḥ before g-→-o.

sentences.t:
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति ।
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
sentences.tr:
na anyam guṇebhyaḥ kartāram yadā draṣṭā anupaśyati |
guṇebhyaḥ ca param vetti mad-bhāvam saḥ adhigacchati ||

morph.gloss: not (na+anyam→nānyam, a+a→ā)
other (acc. sg. masc., object of anupaśyati, agreeing with kartāram)
the guṇas, kept untranslated (abl. pl. 'apart from, other than the guṇas')
to do, act (kartṛ, agent noun 'agent, doer': kartāram, acc. sg. masc., object of anupaśyati)
when (relative adverb)
to see (draṣṭṛ, agent noun 'seer': draṣṭā, nom. sg. masc., subject; draṣṭā+anupaśyati→draṣṭānupaśyati, ā+a→ā)
to perceive, observe (anupaśyati: present 3rd sg. 'perceives')
the guṇas, kept untranslated (abl. pl. 'beyond the guṇas'; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
the beyond, the higher [reality] (acc. sg. neut., object of vetti)
to know (vetti: present 3rd sg. 'knows')
me, my (stem form of aham, first compound member)
state, nature, being (mad-bhāva: 'my own state/being', acc. sg., object of adhigacchati)
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
to attain, reach (adhigacchati: present 3rd sg. 'attains')

sentences.l: No other than-the-guṇas as-agent when the-seer perceives, and beyond-the-guṇas what he knows — he attains my-state-of-being.
sentences.i: When the seer perceives no agent other than the guṇas, and knows what lies beyond the guṇas, he attains to my own state of being.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's third movement (verses 19-20), the promise of liberation through discernment: whoever, as draṣṭā, 'the seer', sees no kartāram anyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ, 'agent other than the guṇas' (i.e. recognizes that all action belongs to the guṇas' interplay, not to the self, as already taught at 3.27 and 13.29), and further vetti guṇebhyaḥ param, 'knows what is beyond the guṇas' (the untouched self), reaches mad-bhāvam, 'my own state of being' — the very promise already made in these terms at 13.18. Sandhi: nānyaṃ is na+anyam (a+a→ā); draṣṭānupaśyati is draṣṭā+anupaśyati (ā+a→ā); guṇebhyaśca is guṇebhyaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); so'dhigacchati is saḥ+adhigacchati (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।
जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
sentences.tr:
guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān |
janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhaiḥ vimuktaḥ amṛtam aśnute ||

morph.gloss: the guṇas, kept untranslated (guṇān: acc. pl. masc., object of atītya)
this (etān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with guṇān; guṇān+etān simply written joined)
to transcend, go beyond (atītya: gerund 'having transcended'; etān+atītya simply written joined)
three (trīn: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with guṇān etān; simply written joined with the following word, the final -n unaffected before the consonant d-)
the embodied one, the soul (nom. sg. masc., subject)
body (first compound member)
arisen, originating (samudbhava: 'arisen from', deha-samudbhava: 'arising from the body', acc. pl. masc., agreeing with guṇān etān trīn)
birth (first compound member)
death (second member)
old age (third member)
pain, suffering (janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkha: instr. pl. 'by/from birth, death, old age, and suffering'; -aiḥ+v-→-air v-)
freed, released (vimukta: past participle, nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
the deathless, immortality (amṛtam: acc. sg. neut., object of aśnute; simply written joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to attain, partake of (aśnute: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains')

sentences.l: These three guṇas having transcended, the-embodied-one, arisen-from-the-body, from-birth-death-old-age-and-suffering freed, immortality attains.
sentences.i: Having transcended these three guṇas that arise from the body, the embodied soul is freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, and attains immortality.
sentences.n: This closes the third movement with the chapter's central promise: the dehī, 'embodied one', having atītya, 'transcended', the trīn guṇān etān, 'these three guṇas' — themselves deha-samudbhavān, 'arising from the body' (from embodiment in nature, not from the true self) — becomes vimuktaḥ, 'freed', from janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhaiḥ, 'birth, death, old age, and suffering' (the standard fourfold formula for saṃsāra, echoing 13.8's janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam), and aśnute, 'attains', amṛtam, immortality — setting up Arjuna's question, in the next verse, about what such transcendence looks like from outside. Sandhi: guṇān etān atītya and trīn dehī each simply write a final nasal joined across the word-boundary; the fused second-line compound packs duḥkhaiḥ+vimuktaḥ (-aiḥ+v-→-air v-) and vimuktaḥ+amṛtam (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.l: By-what marks, these-three-guṇas-transcended, is-one, O Lord? What [is his] conduct, and how does-he-go-beyond these-three-guṇas?
sentences.i: By what marks, Lord, is one known who has gone beyond these three guṇas? What is his conduct, and how does he transcend them?
sentences.n: Arjuna's question, prompted directly by verse 20's promise, opens the chapter's final movement (verses 21-27): he asks for liṅgaiḥ, 'marks, signs' by which such a person could be recognized, ācāraḥ, '[his] conduct', and the manner (katham) of his transcendence — three questions Kṛṣṇa's answer (verses 22-26) addresses roughly in turn. Sandhi: kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto packs kaiḥ+liṅgaiḥ (-aiḥ+l-→-air l-), liṅgaiḥ+trīn (-aiḥ+t-→-ais t-), and atītaḥ+bhavati (-aḥ before bh-→-o); kim ācāraḥ is simply written joined; caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate packs ca+etān (a+e→ai) and etān+trīn (-n+t-→-ṃs t-).

न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥

na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati ||

morph.gloss: light, illumination (prakāśa: acc. sg. masc., object understood with dveṣṭi/kāṅkṣati across the verse)
and
activity, engagement (pravṛtti: acc. sg. fem.)
and

and

not

to desire, long for (kāṅkṣati: present 3rd sg. 'desires')

sentences.l: Illumination, and activity, and delusion indeed, O Pāṇḍava — he hates-not [them] arisen, nor ceased desires.
sentences.i: One who neither hates illumination, activity, and delusion when they have arisen, nor desires them when they have ceased, Pāṇḍava —
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's answer begins here and runs through verse 25. Prakāśa, pravṛtti, and moha, 'illumination, activity, and delusion', name sattva's, rajas's, and tamas's characteristic effects already defined at verses 11-13; the guṇātīta neither dveṣṭi, 'hates', them saṃpravṛttāni, 'when they have arisen', nor kāṅkṣati, 'desires', them nivṛttāni, 'when they have ceased' — indifference to the guṇas' coming and going, not their suppression, is the mark Arjuna asked for. This clause has no subject of its own yet; it is completed by the relative yaḥ, 'who', that opens verse 23. Sandhi: mohameva is moham+eva, simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel.

sentences.t:
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते ।

guṇāḥ vartante iti eva yaḥ avatiṣṭhati na iṅgate ||

like, as (suffix, udāsīna-vat: 'like one indifferent'; -t+ā-→-d ā-)

the guṇas, kept untranslated (instr. pl., agent of vicālyate; -aiḥ+y-→-air y-)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, subject)
not

the guṇas, kept untranslated (nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ before v-→-ā)
to operate, function, go on (vartante: present middle 3rd pl. 'operate'; here in the shortened epic/'chāndasa' form vartanta for vartante before iti, an archaic usage noted already by Śaṅkara)
thus, '[merely] that' (quotation particle; iti+eva→ity eva, -i+e-→-y e-)
only, merely

to stand firm, abide, remain (avatiṣṭhati: present 3rd sg. 'remains, abides')
not (na+iṅgate→neṅgate, a+i→e)

sentences.l: As-if-indifferent seated, by-the-guṇas who is not moved; '[merely] the-guṇas operate' — thus, who abides, does-not-waver.
sentences.i: he sits as if indifferent, unmoved by the guṇas; who abides thinking only 'it is the guṇas that are operating', and does not waver —
sentences.n: This continues verse 22's description with the sentence's main relative clauses: udāsīna-vat āsīnaḥ, 'seated as if indifferent/neutral' (a memorable image of studied detachment), guṇaiḥ na vicālyate, 'not moved by the guṇas', and abiding in the settled understanding guṇāḥ vartante iti eva, '[it is] merely [that] the guṇas operate' — restating verse 19's own insight that the guṇas alone act — and so neṅgate, 'does not waver, stir'. Vartanta, the verb form used here, is a shortened epic ('chāndasa', Vedic-style) form of vartante before iti, already noted as such by Śaṅkara. Sandhi: guṇair yo is guṇaiḥ+yaḥ (-aiḥ+y-→-air y-); ity eva is iti+eva (-i+e-→-y e-); yo'vatiṣṭhati is yaḥ+avatiṣṭhati (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); neṅgate is na+iṅgate (a+i→e).

gold (sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcana: 'regarding a clod, a stone, and gold as equal', nom. sg. masc.)

sentences.l: Equal-in-pain-and-pleasure, self-abiding, regarding-clod-stone-and-gold-as-equal, equal-toward-the-pleasant-and-unpleasant, steady, equal-to-blame-and-self-praise —
sentences.i: equal in pain and pleasure, self-possessed, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold alike; equal toward the pleasant and unpleasant, steady, equal to blame and to praise of himself —
sentences.n: The description continues with a run of compounds naming the guṇātīta's equanimity toward every ordinary pair of opposites — pain and pleasure, a clod of earth, a stone, and gold treated alike, the pleasant and the unpleasant, blame and self-praise — generalizing the equanimity already commended at 2.38 and 12.18-19. Svastha, 'self-abiding, self-possessed' (literally 'standing in oneself'), names the ground of this equanimity: rooted in the self, not in the guṇas' fluctuations. Sandhi: loṣṭāśma- is loṣṭa+aśma (a+a→ā); priyāpriyo is priya+apriya (a+a→ā), with the compound's own -aḥ before dh-→-o; nindātma- is nindā+ātma (ā+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥

māna-apamānayoḥ tulyaḥ tulyaḥ mitra-ari-pakṣayoḥ |

dishonor, disrespect (māna-apamāna: 'honor and dishonor', gen./loc. dual — the vulgate reading, followed here; the BORI critical edition reads mānāvamānayoḥ, with avamāna, a near-synonym of apamāna, in its place: 'honor and disrespect' — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint)

sentences.l: Equal in-honor-and-dishonor, equal toward-the-sides-of-friend-and-foe, one-who-has-abandoned-all-undertakings — gone-beyond-the-guṇas, he, is called.
sentences.i: equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward the side of friend and of foe alike, having given up every undertaking — such a one is said to have gone beyond the guṇas.
sentences.n: This completes the description of the guṇātīta begun at verse 22: equal to māna and apamāna, 'honor and dishonor', and to mitra and ari, 'friend and foe', he is sarva-ārambha-parityāgī, 'one who has abandoned every undertaking' (not inaction as such, but freedom from the driven initiative that is rajas's own mark at verse 12's ārambhaḥ) — guṇa-atītaḥ, 'gone beyond the guṇas', exactly the state Arjuna asked about at verse 21. The vulgate reading, followed here, is māna-apamānayoḥ, 'of honor and dishonor'; the BORI critical edition reads mānāvamānayoḥ instead, with avamāna (a near-synonym of apamāna, both meaning 'disrespect, dishonor') in its place — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint, and not a difference of sense. Sandhi: mānāpamānayoḥ is māna+apamānayoḥ (a+a→ā), the whole compound's own -oḥ+t-→-os t- before the first tulyaḥ, whose own -aḥ+t-→-as t- precedes the second tulyaḥ, whose own -aḥ before m-→-o; sarvārambha- is sarva+ārambha (a+ā→ā); guṇātītaḥ is guṇa+atīta (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥

sa guṇān samatītya etān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate ||

devotion (first compound member)
yoga, discipline (bhakti-yoga: 'the yoga/discipline of devotion', instr. sg.)
to serve, worship, honor (sevate: present middle 3rd sg. 'serves')

this (etān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with guṇān; etān+brahma-bhūyāya simply written joined, the final -n unaffected before the consonant b-)

sentences.l: And who me with-unwavering-devotion, with-the-yoga-of-devotion, serves — he, these-guṇas having-fully-transcended, for-the-state-of-being-brahman becomes fit.
sentences.i: And whoever serves me with unwavering devotion, through the yoga of devotion, transcends these guṇas entirely and becomes fit for the state of being brahman.
sentences.n: This closes the description of the guṇātīta by adding what the preceding, more austere account (verses 22-25) has not yet mentioned: bhakti, devotion. One who sevate, 'serves', Kṛṣṇa avyabhicāreṇa bhakti-yogena, 'with unwavering devotion, through the yoga of devotion' (the same insistence on undivided constancy as 12.6's ananyena eva yogena and 13.10's ananya-yogena), and samatītya, 'having fully transcended', the guṇas, becomes fit brahma-bhūyāya, 'for the state of being brahman' — the same term, brahma-bhūya, that names the culmination of the whole poem's teaching at 18.53, here reached through devotion rather than the discernment of verses 19-23 alone. Sandhi: yo'vyabhicāreṇa is yaḥ+avyabhicāreṇa (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); guṇānsamatītyaitān packs guṇān+samatītya (simply joined before the consonant s-) and samatītya+etān (a+e→ai), running on, still joined, into brahmabhūyāya.

शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥

śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasya aikāntikasya ca ||

and

and

sentences.l: Of-brahman, for, [I am] the-foundation, I, of-the-immortal and of-the-imperishable, and; of-the-eternal and of-dharma, of-absolute-happiness, and.
sentences.i: For I am the foundation of brahman — of the immortal and the imperishable, of the eternal dharma, and of unmixed happiness.
sentences.n: The chapter closes with Kṛṣṇa's own self-declaration as pratiṣṭhā, 'foundation, resting-place', of brahman itself — a striking claim that reverses the more usual direction of chapters 13-14 (where brahman has stood as the ultimate ground, e.g. 13.12-17, and Kṛṣṇa's relation to it stated more modestly at 13.12's mat-param) by making Kṛṣṇa the support of brahman, of amṛta and avyaya, 'the immortal and the imperishable', of śāśvata dharma (dharma kept untranslated per convention), and of sukham aikāntikam, 'unmixed, absolute happiness' — four genitives in apposition gathering everything ultimate the poem has so far named, all grounded, this verse claims, in Kṛṣṇa himself. It closes the chapter on a note that prepares the still bolder claims about Kṛṣṇa's relation to every being and every path made in chapter 18. Sandhi: pratiṣṭhāhaṃ is pratiṣṭhā+aham (ā+a→ā); ahamamṛtasyāvyayasya packs aham+amṛtasya (simply joined before the vowel) and amṛtasya+avyayasya (a+a→ā); sukhasyaikāntikasya is sukhasya+aikāntikasya (a+ai→ai).

about: Chapter 14, the Yoga of the Threefold Division of the Guṇas (Guṇatrayavibhāgayoga), continues directly from chapter 13 with no question from Arjuna, as Kṛṣṇa promises to declare once more the supreme knowledge that has carried every sage before him to the highest perfection. He opens with a brief cosmogony — the great brahman as his womb, into which he places the seed from which every form in every realm arises — before turning to the chapter's central teaching: the three guṇas, sattva, rajas, and tamas, the constituent qualities of nature that bind the otherwise imperishable embodied self to the body. He defines each in turn: sattva as stainless and luminous, yet binding through attachment to happiness and to knowledge; rajas as passionate, born of craving, binding through attachment to action; tamas as born of ignorance, binding through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep. He describes how the three constantly contend for supremacy, the visible symptoms of each one's ascendancy, the destiny after death and the fruits of action and knowledge proper to each, and a ranked cosmology in which those who abide in sattva rise, those of rajas remain in the middle, and those of tamas sink down. True knowledge, he says, is to see that the guṇas alone act and to know what lies beyond them — the knowledge that frees the embodied soul from birth, death, old age, and suffering and grants immortality. Arjuna then asks how one who has gone beyond the three guṇas can be recognized, and Kṛṣṇa answers with a portrait of such a person: indifferent alike to the presence or absence of illumination, activity, and delusion; equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth and gold, in blame and praise, in honor and dishonor, in friend and foe; and one who has given up every self-driven undertaking. He adds that whoever serves him with unwavering devotion crosses beyond the guṇas by that devotion alone and becomes fit for the state of being brahman. The chapter closes with Kṛṣṇa's declaration of himself as the very foundation of brahman — of the immortal and the imperishable, of the eternal dharma, and of unmixed happiness.
